analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the canonical definition index and selected details. ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift:17-19 now records request arrival on a connected socket; :31-44 delegates refusal recovery to ServingReadiness, suppresses reconnects with no advertised models, and resets retry state for an authorized verdict. Connection reconstruction at :10-12 clears the optional request timestamp. Recovery still consults busy/update state before requesting reconnect (:54-70). Service/DaemonStateFile.swift's head patch at :338-345 adds only an optional activity timestamp, not prompt content, credentials or proof; existing atomic diagnostic persistence is unchanged (base :637-655). ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:155-169 accepts an internal receive timestamp while retaining the wall-clock default and diagnostic persistence; connection authorization clearing remains at :147-152.
No concrete security regression is established by this scope. The main affected contracts are TB-002/TB-011, T-052/T-053/T-057 and A-016/A-018: evidence of routing must not become serving permission or extend an Apple grant. No supplied change alters encryption, attestation verification, cache isolation (T-041), billing counters, privileged fan authority or add-on authentication.
Integration must inspect ServingReadiness.verdict and the callers of noteCoordinatorRequest/handleTrustStatus: confirm request timestamps are socket-scoped, receive times cannot be supplied by adversarial message fields, and stale requests or refusals cannot defeat recovery or authorization expiry. Also verify requestPlannedReconnect closes admission and preserves cancellation/hold behavior; comments alone do not establish that contract. These implementations and call sites are outside the supplied scope, so their absence is a coverage limit, not a finding.
